text:
ryan: Heads-up — after merging the kernel-selector v3 change yesterday we saw a steady uptick in p99 for small-batch chat on T4 pools. Investigating if batching heuristics are interacting poorly with new fallthrough paths.
anya: Noted. Do we have a repro that isolates A) kernel fallthroughs B) kv-fragmentation C) batch formation?
simon: I ran a local replay of the nightly workload against kernel-selector:v3. Quick findings: H100/A100 unchanged, but A10/T4 payloads flip to a slower kernel ~30% of the time on short sequences (~32-128 tokens). That correlates with p99 regressions.
lina: I also see more KV cache fragmentation on mixed-length traces — more cache misses cause additional kernel switch overhead. Perf dump attached (trimmed):
```
# perf-sample
model: redwood-7b
device: a10
seq: median=64 p95=128
kernel_path: fast_attention -> fallback_attention (30% runs)
kv_hit_rate: 0.72 -> 0.55 after selector change
latency_p99: 128ms -> 170ms
```
ryan: Thanks. Two quick questions: 1) Are batch formation policies sending more uneven slices? 2) Did default max_tokens_per_batch change anywhere?
anya: For (1) yes — the new slice-priority heuristic favors earlier requests which created thinner batches on T4 under bursty traffic. For (2) nope global defaults unchanged, but kernel-specific token caps (we added dynamic ceiling hints) are higher for A100/H100 and slightly lower for L4/T4.
simon: Hypothesis: On A10/T4 the selector chooses a cheaper kernel that expects dense packing; when batches are thin it costs more because of per-call overhead. We should consider lowering token_budget_target for T4/A10 and temporarily pin kernel-selector to v2 for critical pods.
lina: Agreed. Proposed quick mitigation config (can be rolled via rollout):
```
{"per_gpu_token_budget": {"a10": 6000, "t4": 4500, "l4": 7000, "a100": 14000, "h100": 16000}, "slice_min_size": 16, "slice_max_size": 256}
```
ryan: That looks reasonable. Also add a short window to prefer kernel v2 for devices where kv_hit_rate < 0.6 to avoid fallthrough churn.
anya: I can patch the router policy: if kv_hit_rate < 0.6 and avg_batch_width < 8 -> prefer kernel-v2; else kernel-selector:v3. Quick A/B canary to 5% of T4 fleet.
simon: Ran a canary sim with those budgets: p99 reduced from 170ms -> 135ms, throughput ~+4% for T4. KV hit rate also improved to ~0.66. No visible impact on A100/H100.
perf-bot: nightly-regression-check: after canary deployed to 5% T4 (2024-11-09T03:00Z) observed 4.1% p99 reduction cluster-wide on affected nodes. No error-rate increase.
lina: Good. Plan: a) roll these token budgets to 25% T4/A10 b) add router rule for kv_hit gating c) add a short-term heuristic to reduce slice-priority bias during burst windows. Rollout notes in PR #4872.
ryan: Also flag for follow-up: run more microbench profiles to see if kernel v3 micro-path could be optimized for low-width batches (maybe remove an allocation on fallback path). Opening perf ticket.
anya: I'll schedule targeted profiles for each device class (a10/t4/l4/a100/h100) and export kernel call traces + allocation flamegraphs. ETA EOD.
simon: Thanks — will coordinate on the PR and test infra. If we keep regressions low we can keep selector v3 with these tuning knobs. :thumbsup:
ryan: Perfect. TL;DR: immediate token_budget tweak + router kv gating -> canary shows p99 improvement on T4/A10; next: kernel micro-optimizations for narrow batches and KV packing improvements.
